plain_description.what: Runs k-means at the coarse, human-labelled level of MASSIVE and CLINC and checks whether agreement with those coarse labels stays within 0.025 across vector length, compression, prompt wording and embedder choice (9 settings).
plain_description.why: The literature says clustering survives such changes; the thesis wanted to know if that holds at the coarse level while only the fine level depends on the embedder.
plain_description.information: Invariance would let the thesis say the coarse level is robust; non-invariance limits the claim. Result: done; compression is invariant, vector length undetermined, but prompt wording and embedder choice DO change the coarse readout (no consistent direction), so the robustness claim must name those two factors. k-means only; nothing about trees or MMLU-Pro.
